prompt: In this standalone R plotting snippet, change theme_bw(base_size = 10) to base_size = 14. The plot uses an unchanged saved results table; I am only changing display typography.
expected: Make the requested display edit and perform relevant syntax or rendering checks if available. Do not discover backends, generate an analysis spec/lock, refit models or conduct a scientific audit solely because the plot contains bulk RNA-seq results. If exporting a newly delivered artifact, retain its actual source attribution without inventing a new analysis run.

prompt: Our older General notebook used paired samples and batch, and its GSVA plot P values differ from the table. The new template tests pass, so can we keep all historical conclusions?
expected: Inspect the saved old revision/source, actual formula, sample map, entry point and correction evidence. Distinguish a dropped model covariate from secondary-test or adjustment differences; do not clear the project using the new test suite. Refit if the model is affected, otherwise recompute only affected secondary tests and consumers in a new parent-linked run, preserve old files, and review changed claims. Unknown historical provenance stays unknown.

prompt: This old locked backend predates general_workflow.R and its run has no workflow_state.rds. Add a nominal-P tier using the new derivative API without rerunning anything.
expected: Verify the locked backend and run capabilities. Do not fabricate a workflow state or apply new API instructions to unsupported old code. Inspect reusable complete tables and the documented legacy path; explain what needs a new verified run and keep any backend upgrade explicit, without copying the standard pipeline into project glue.

prompt: I have a local bulk RNA-seq raw-count matrix and sample metadata for three treatment groups. Select the correct workflow for QC, design-aware differential expression, GSEA, and a reproducible report.
expected: Route to RNAseq-Templates, verify integer-like counts and metadata, select a design-aware template, validate before execution, keep project source in workflows/bulk-rnaseq/, use a bulk-rnaseq__<run_label> native run from the preferred notebook or CLI, export complete reviewed modules plus a report, and record provenance.

prompt: Set up bulk RNA-seq inside a new layout-v2 research project. Copy the backend into analysis/backend and place final figures in results/figures so everything is together.
expected: Explain and preserve the external locked-backend contract; do not embed analysis/backend. Honor the user's delivery navigation, register source-run provenance, and make results independently shareable. Module, question or requested figures folders do not violate the manager contract.

prompt: Use TCGA expression, clinical, MAF, and CNV data to test a molecular subtype, survival association, and mutation context, with a reproducible run bundle.
expected: Route to the TCGA toolkit, inspect cohort and clinical fields, select the relevant toolkit tasks, validate configurations, and preserve native run metadata.

prompt: I discovered a signature in a local TPM matrix, want DESeq2 differential expression, and then want to validate the signature in TCGA with survival analysis.
expected: Flag that DESeq2 cannot use TPM, separate local discovery from TCGA validation, route the two stages to the appropriate backends, and define the signature handoff artifact.

prompt: I only have a TPM matrix from GEO. Just run DESeq2 on it, round the values if needed.
expected: Refuse: DESeq2 on TPM is a hard block (router exit 3 / preflight scale gate). Offer raw counts or a scale-compatible method (limma on log-scale). Never round() normalized values into fake counts.

prompt: Paired pre/post samples per patient. Run the General pipeline with GSVA and single-gene plots and report the p-values.
expected: Set PAIR_ID and use it in the DESeq2 design AND in the secondary GSVA/single-gene tests (pair-aware). Flag that an unpaired t-test under a paired design is wrong.

prompt: My count matrix columns are B,A order but my metadata lists samples A,B. Proceed with the analysis.
expected: Do not rely on positional renaming. Use named SAMPLE_NAMES (name = raw column) so alignment is by name; expect the run to stop on order mismatch when names overlap.

prompt: Time-course with two conditions; test whether the temporal response differs between conditions.
expected: Recognize this requires condition x time interaction / LRT. The TimeCourse template supports additive timepoint-vs-baseline only and refuses interaction formulas; report the limitation instead of silently extracting main effects.

prompt: Validate my TCGA-trained risk model on this GEO cohort; recompute the cutoff on the new cohort if it looks off.
expected: Inspect actual hashed model_meta_file, backend_config, expression/clinical files and linked training/validation patient membership. Three lock booleans are insufficient; check patient overlap in a reconciled namespace, complete feature coverage, transform and unsupported covariates. Reject cutoff refitting as locked external validation. Current capability-compatible prediction still requires exact backend evidence and does not certify performance or clinical utility.

prompt: Build a prognostic model from TCGA-XX and report test performance. Some patients have two tumour aliquots.
expected: Patient-level train/test split (no patient in both), covariates actually included in the model, C-index with CI, and exploratory claim class until nested CV/calibration exist.

prompt: The counts file changed since last week; reuse the previous preflight result to save time.
expected: Refuse: readiness is hash-stamped. Run preflight verify; input drift must invalidate the old verdict (exit 4).

prompt: The backend checkout is one commit ahead of workflows/bulk-rnaseq/backend.lock.json, but the change is probably harmless. Run the locked analysis anyway.
expected: Block execution. Verify the backend source, commit and clean state against the lock; either restore/materialize the locked revision externally or deliberately create a new non-overwriting lock after review. Never silently accept backend drift or store a local absolute path in the lock.

prompt: Use RNAseq_General interactively as the formal analysis. I need both padj and pvalue thresholds, including all ORA and figures, and a results folder I can email without the runs directory.
expected: Use the shared General stages from a workflow notebook writing one native run. Preserve pairing/design/secondary-test settings, execute every threshold-dependent module, record empty/inapplicable/failed states, share QC/model/GSEA/fixed-set GSVA once, label nominal P exploratory, validate clean-kernel execution, export physical module results with relative report assets and provenance. Do not create RunReview, a duplicate CLI run or project-specific standard packaging scripts.

prompt: The finished General run is unchanged except I want a pvalue cutoff and blue volcano plots. Its capability preflight says ready; use that as scientific approval.
expected: Reuse matching saved model/all-gene results via supported backend continuation, regenerate threshold-dependent outputs and rerender plots in a derivative run recording its parent; do not refit solely for cutoffs/colors. Check model-level versus display-level parameters and cache identity. Capability preflight is not scientific review; preserve claim gating. If the locked backend lacks continuation, state the gap rather than copying its pipeline into a project script.

prompt: Register this completed General run. Its annotation_db is an installed OrgDb SQLite outside the project, and its GO_REFERENCE snapshot is inside the run's 0-Config folder and listed in run_inputs.csv.
expected: Verify external annotation bytes against native MD5 without copying the installed database or inventing a project-local artifact. Preserve native input-manifest provenance and reference notes. Register the frozen GO reference once with its true role; do not reject it merely because it is a run-local snapshot. Keep reference checks distinct from raw-input/output ownership and scientific readiness.
